sec:surreal-appendix-intro:
Motivation: a surreal-number ambient for QOU.

This appendix explores a speculative lift of the Quantum Observable Universe from its native ground field \mathbb{R} (or \mathbb{C}) to Conway's surreal numbers \mathbf{No} — the unique proper-class real-closed field containing every ordered-field extension of \mathbb{R}, including the hyperreals ^{*}\mathbb{R}, the ordinals \mathrm{Ord}, and all Hahn series \mathbb{R}((t^{G})) [conway1976, ehrlich2012].

Nothing in this appendix alters this paper. The Quantum Observable Universe is developed and proved over \mathbb{R}. This appendix offers an ambient field into which the archimedean content embeds and from which it is recovered via standard-part. The claims here are either remarks interpreting existing blocks, conjectures pending further development, or definitions of new auxiliary structures.

Motivation for the surreal lift

Four distinct uses motivate the lift:

  1. An explicit ambient for q \to 1 limits. Setting q = 1 + \varepsilon for an infinitesimal \varepsilon \in \mathbf{No} replaces the (classically broken) classical-limit functor (classical limit functor) with the evaluation at a specific surreal, composed with Robinson's standard-part map [robinson1966]. The classical regime becomes a quotient, not a limit.

  2. A grading source aligned with braid combinatorics. Gonshor's sign-sequence presentation of \mathbf{No} [gonshor1986] assigns every surreal a function \alpha \to \{+,-\} for some ordinal \alpha. The Hecke generator \sigma has two eigenvalues (q and -q^{-1}), so a braid word decorated with eigenspace choices produces a sign sequence and therefore a surreal number.

  3. Named values for blow-ups and singularities. The Möbius energy integral, renormalisation scales, and hyperbolic-volume divergences become honest elements of \mathbf{No} (infinite surreals like \omega, \omega^2) rather than informal symbols \infty. Counterterms become named negative surreals.

  4. Infinitesimal axioms. Strict equalities in the QOU axioms (Frobenius pairing = \mathrm{id}; observability cohomology = 0; vacuum = 0) can be relaxed to hold up to an infinitesimal. The archimedean theory is recovered by taking standard-parts; the surreal theory is strictly stronger (carries information about the infinitesimal deviation).

Lossiness of the lift

A first-pass survey suggests that replacing \mathbb{R} with \mathbf{No} must give up Lebesgue measure, Hilbert-space completions, and hyperbolic geometry. But an honest survey of the QOU development shows most of these are never actually used in a load-bearing way:

  • Lebesgue measure enters only the Möbius energy integral (one block). Everywhere else, "integrals" are categorical (Frobenius counit) or reduce to rational/algebraic formulas.
  • Hilbert completion appears in exactly one proof passage, where the only step invoking completion is the word "dense" — which can be replaced by "spans the algebraic direct limit" without loss.
  • Hausdorff dimension is given by the rational formula d_H(q) = (2q-1)^2/q^3, so it transfers to \mathbf{No} exactly.
  • Spectral theorems are never used; Hoefsmit's seminormal form diagonalises Hecke generators algebraically over \mathbb{Q}(q^{1/2}).

The only obstructions that genuinely bite are the Möbius energy integral and the hyperbolic-volume side of the Kashaev comparison. This paper's mass-formula pipeline — Hoefsmit \to Markov trace \to Jones polynomial \to categorical mass — transfers to \mathbf{No} unchanged.

Non-goals

This appendix does not:

  • claim a physical interpretation of non-archimedean values (the work is purely mathematical);
  • replace any main-text proof (this paper's results stand on their own over \mathbb{R});
  • solve the Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture;
  • construct a canonical Lebesgue-like measure on \mathbf{No} (it has none; the appendix sidesteps this rather than solving it).

Structure of the appendix

Section 1 states the algebraic core that survives unchanged; Section 2 lists the analytic obstructions; Section 3 shows what survives of calculus up to infinitesimals. Sections 4--5 construct the birthday and sign-sequence gradings and the standard-part functor. Section 6 relaxes the strict QOU axioms. Section 7 gives two speculative reformulations: the aether as a Hahn series, and Kashaev's conjecture as a standard-part identity.
sec:surreal-survives-breaks-intro: The core algebraic structure of the QOU framework survives passage to the surreal numbers. This section identifies which constructions extend and which require analytic continuation.
rem:transcendental-accounting:
Remark Transcendental-accounting ledger: every period in the paper, indexed by Goncharov depth. This section records which periods appear, where, how they relate, and whether their post-archimedean relations are forced by pre-archimedean q-rational structure or are archimedean accidents.

A relation R(\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_m) = 0 in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] on the algebraic side survives under the archimedean realization functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} if and only if it is a q-polynomial identity. A relation that holds only among the archimedean values \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\alpha_i) \in \mathbb{R} but not among the \alpha_i \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}] is an archimedean accident. The 5-term Bloch–Wigner relation among hyperbolic volumes is a typical example.

The graded-Mikusiński correspondence (GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence) predicts the origin of each relation by depth. The table below operationalises this for every period in the QOU paper.

See Table.

The table makes two structural facts visible:

Fact 1: depth-2 ceiling for hyperbolic 3-mfd volumes. Every hyperbolic 3-manifold volume in the paper occurs at depth 2 (one \mathrm{Li}_2 factor). The Bloch–Wigner formula \mathrm{Vol}(M) = \sum_i D(z_i) over an ideal-tetrahedron triangulation forces this. Escaping depth 2 requires a different invariant: \mathrm{CS}, hyperbolic 4-manifolds, or the trilogarithm at algebraic points (the bring-trilog-zeta5 route).

Fact 2: pre-archimedean q-rational relations imply post-archimedean equalities. For any two Bring-embeddable knots K, K', if J_K(q) = J_{K'}(q) in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}], then \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K'). The volume \mathrm{Vol} is computed from J_K^{(N)} via a limit depending only on the polynomial. Whether this implication is vacuous (whether there are no Jones-coincident pairs among Bring-embeddable knots) remains open (Exhaustiveness of the QOU knots in the Descartes space (open) Question 3). A single Jones-coincident pair yields a non-trivial post-archimedean equality forced by q-rational structure—exactly the wall-crossing prediction the correspondence makes explicit.

Non-surviving relations: archimedean accidents. The 5-term Bloch–Wigner relation

D(x) + D(y) + D\!\left(\tfrac{1-x}{1-xy}\right) + D(1 - xy) + D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y}{1-xy}\right) = 0

holds among hyperbolic volumes after \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} but is not a \mathbb{Q}(q)-polynomial identity on the pre-archimedean side. It is an archimedean accident at depth 2: a relation in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1 with no q-polynomial witness.

Similar wall-crossing accidents occur at depth 3:

  • Goncharov's 22-term relation for \mathrm{Li}_3 at 5th roots.
  • Euler's 1775 identity \zeta(2,1) = \zeta(3) (an accident from the algebraic side, since the multiple zeta value \zeta(2,1) is a separate iterated integral that evaluates to the single zeta).

Open question: post-archimedean structure forced by Bring's S_5. Because Bring's curve has S_5 symmetry, the cyclotomic field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) acts on the Bring-natural depth-3 grouplikes. The Galois action \sigma_a \colon \zeta_5 \mapsto \zeta_5^a for \gcd(a, 5) = 1 permutes:

\{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5),\, \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^2),\, \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^3),\, \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^4)\}.

The orbit-sum identity for the trilogarithm over the fifth roots of unity, verified numerically, is the Galois-invariant trace of this S_5-action. The Galois-non-invariant components—individual \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) values—give a 4-dimensional \mathbb{Q}-vector space of depth-3 periods on which S_5 acts irreducibly. These are the depth-3 Bring-natural transcendentals. Their post-archimedean structure (linear relations over \overline{\mathbb{Q}}) is governed by the motivic Galois group, not by the q-rational pre-image. This gives a concrete instance of post-archimedean structure not visible at the q-polynomial level.

Upper bounds on the span at a given weight and level (literature). The ledger indexes periods by depth but records no upper bound on how many of them can be \mathbb{Q}-independent. For multiple polylogarithm values at N-th roots of unity of weight w, let d(w,N) be the dimension of their \mathbb{Q}-span. Deligne and Goncharov give d(w,N) \le D(w,N), where D(w,N) are the coefficients of an explicit generating function depending only on Euler's totient \varphi(N) and the number of prime factors of N [zhao2008-mpl-roots-of-unity, Prop. 1]. A dimension stated in this ledger, such as the four-dimensional span of the individual \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) above, is an independence claim and so a lower bound; D(w,N) is the matching upper bound that a PSLQ basis at that weight and level cannot exceed. The bound is not evaluated here. The same source shows that Racinet's standard relations (double shuffle, distribution and weight-one relations) do not exhaust the \mathbb{Q}-linear relations: at weight 3 and level 4 they give only d(3,4) \le 9, one more than the Deligne–Goncharov bound, and the missing relation is derived from the octahedral symmetry of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus (\{0,\infty\} \cup \mu_4) [zhao2008-mpl-roots-of-unity, §1]. Level 4 is the level of Catalan's constant G = \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/2) in the ledger's table; the extra relation sits one weight higher, at weight 3, and comes from a symmetry of the punctured line rather than from the standard list.

prop:borel-partial-resolution:
Proposition Borel's theorem partially discharges the depth correspondence's sharpness target — explicit dimensions. The depth correspondence (GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence) asserts both an inclusion and a sharpness condition. Via the K-theory translation (K-theory \leftrightarrow depth filtration Rosetta), the sharpness condition factors through Borel's theorem on the algebraic K-theory of number fields. This proposition records the explicit Borel dimensions for each Bring-natural number field.

Theorem (Borel 1977). Let F be a number field with r_1 real embeddings and r_2 pairs of complex embeddings. Then for n \geq 2:

\dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \bigl( K_{2n-1}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \bigr) =
\begin{cases}
  r_1 + r_2 & \text{if } n \text{ even}, \\
  r_2 & \text{if } n \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}

The same formula holds for the indecomposable part K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}.

Each Bring-embeddable knot K has a shape parameter z_K \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times generating a number field F_K = \mathbb{Q}(z_K). The Borel rank gives the minimum dimension of the Beilinson regulator image at depth n.

See Table 1.

At depth 2 (figure-8 row), Borel's theorem gives \dim_\mathbb{Q} K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 1. The Bloch–Wigner regulator maps this injectively after rationalisation. The image is exactly the \mathbb{Q}-line spanned by \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3). Inclusion and sharpness hold at depth 2 over \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6). The depth-2 case of the depth correspondence is a theorem at the figure-8 row.

At depth 3 (Bring trilog row), Borel's theorem gives \dim_\mathbb{Q} K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)) \otimes \mathbb{Q} = 2. The Goncharov regulator maps this rank-2 space to \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2. The Bring trilog witness (Bring trilog at \zeta_5 as depth-3 grouplike value (50-digit functional-equation cross-validated witness)) provides 4 grouplike values \{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) : k = 1,2,3,4\}. Modulo the orbit-sum relation, these span a \mathbb{Q}-vector space of exact rank 2, matching Borel's prediction. Whether the entire \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2 over \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) is generated is Beilinson's conjecture.

Borel's theorem gives explicit Borel-rank lower bounds on the dimension of \tau_\mathrm{arch}(G^{(n)}) in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} for every Bring-natural number field. It does not provide the upper bound (Beilinson's conjecture).

For the depth correspondence, depth 2 is a theorem. Depth 3 has Borel-rank lower bounds as theorems, leaving Beilinson's conjecture as the remaining piece. Depth \geq 4 is fully Beilinson-conjectural.

prop:depth-2-identification-bloch-suslin:
Proposition Depth-2 identification of G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) with K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} — provable via Bloch--Suslin. Let F be a number field, q \in F generic, and let \mathcal{H}_q be the aether convolution Hopf algebra over F (Frobenius–Hopf aether). The depth-2 identification is:

\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl( G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \big/ \mathcal{P}_1 \bigr)_F \cong K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q},

where the right-hand side carries the Bloch–Suslin regulator K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R} / \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}. This identification is a theorem, with proof chain via the Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(F), Suslin's isomorphism, and the archimedean evaluation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q.

Combined with Borel's theorem partially discharges the depth correspondence's sharpness target — explicit dimensions, depth 2 of GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence is a theorem over every Bring-natural number field F = \mathbb{Q}(z_K). Depth 3 is conditional on Goncharov's motivic conjecture but has all non-Goncharov steps provable. Depth \geq 4 is conditional on Beilinson and Goncharov.
prf:depth-2-identification-bloch-suslin:
Proof Proof of depth-2 identification (Bloch–Suslin). Derivation chain.

Step 1 (Bloch group, Bloch 1978). Define the Bloch group of F:

  \mathfrak{B}(F)
  \;:=\;
  \mathbb{Z}[F^\times \setminus \{1\}] \;/\; \bigl(\text{5-term relations, torsion}\bigr)

where the 5-term relations are

  \{x\}_2 - \{y\}_2 + \left\{\tfrac{y}{x}\right\}_2 - \left\{\tfrac{1 - x^{-1}}{1 - y^{-1}}\right\}_2 + \left\{\tfrac{1 - x}{1 - y}\right\}_2 \;=\; 0

for all x, y \in F^\times with x, y, x/y \neq 1.

The Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm D \colon F \to \mathbb{R} extends \mathbb{Q}-linearly to a well-defined map

  D \;\colon\; \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{R} \big/ \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}

because D satisfies the 5-term relation as a function on F-points (Wigner 1955; Bloch 1978).

Step 2 (Suslin's isomorphism, Suslin 1986). Theorem (Suslin). There is a natural isomorphism of \mathbb{Q}-vector spaces

  K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\cong\;
  \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}

induced by sending the generator \{x\}_2 \in \mathfrak{B}(F) to the corresponding class in K_3^{\mathrm{ind}} via the Bloch–Wigner / Beilinson regulator. The composed map

  K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\;
  \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;D\;}\;
  \mathbb{R} \big/ \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}

is the Bloch–Suslin regulator, and it is injective after tensoring with \mathbb{R} (Borel + Suslin).

Step 3 (archimedean image of G^{(2)}, this paper). The aether convolution algebra \mathcal{H}_q's depth-2 grouplike \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) for z \in F^\times has archimedean image

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Li}_2(z) \pmod{\mathcal{P}_1}

by Uniqueness of the categorical Laplace transform combined with the analytic continuation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q to \mathrm{Li}_2 at q \to 1. The Bloch–Wigner companion

  D(z)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \arg(1-z)\log|z|

is the single-valued version of \mathrm{Li}_2, well-defined modulo \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}. Comparing:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)\bigr) \pmod{\mathcal{P}_1}
  \;\sim\;
  D(z) \pmod{\pi^2 \mathbb{Q}}.

Step 4 (composition). Combining Steps 1–3:

  \begin{array}{rcl}
    G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q)\big|_F \big/ \mathcal{P}_1
    & \xrightarrow{\;\;\tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\;\;} &
    \mathbb{R} / \pi^2 \mathbb{Q} \\
    \downarrow \text{(generated by $\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z),\ z \in F^\times$)} & & \uparrow D \\
    \mathfrak{B}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
    & \xrightarrow[\;\;\sim\;\;]{\text{Suslin}} &
    K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}

prop:b1-soft-sharpness-theorem:
Proposition Soft sharpness of the depth correspondence is theorem-level — via Borel + polylog non-vanishing. Let K be a Bring-embeddable knot with shape parameter z_K \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times \setminus \{0, 1\} and let F = \mathbb{Q}(z_K). For every n \geq 2:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\mathrm{Li}_n^q(z_K)\bigr) \;\not\equiv\; 0 \pmod{\mathcal{P}_{n-1}}.

This is the soft sharpness half of the depth correspondence GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence. The depth-n image \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(G^{(n)}\rvert_F) is non-trivial in \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}. It requires no part of Goncharov's or Beilinson's conjectures.
prf:b1-soft-sharpness-theorem:
Proof Proof of b1 soft sharpness theorem. Step 1 (Borel non-vanishing). By Borel's theorem partially discharges the depth correspondence's sharpness target — explicit dimensions, \dim_\mathbb{Q} K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \geq 1 for n \geq 2 when F is non-trivial cyclotomic (specifically: F = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5), \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_6), \mathbb{Q}(i), all of which have r_2 \geq 1). The Beilinson–Borel regulator

  K_{2n-1}^{\mathrm{ind}}(F) \otimes \mathbb{Q}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathbb{R} / \pi^{2(n-1)} \mathbb{Q}

is injective after tensoring with \mathbb{R} (Borel 1977, Theorem 12.3 — the regulator is rationally injective).

Step 2 (polylog non-vanishing). The single-valued \mathrm{Li}_n companion (Bloch–Wigner D at n = 2, Goncharov D_n for n \geq 3) is non-zero on every algebraic argument z \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times \setminus \{0, 1\} (Lewin 1991, Polylogarithms and Associated Functions §2):

  D_n(z) \;\neq\; 0
  \quad\text{for } z \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times \setminus \{0, 1\}.

Equivalently: no algebraic point is a "regulator zero" of D_n.

Step 3 (composition). Combining Steps 1 and 2:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\mathrm{Li}_n^q(z_K))
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Li}_n(z_K) \pmod{\mathcal{P}_{n-1}}
  \;\sim\;
  D_n(z_K) \neq 0
  \pmod{\mathcal{P}_{n-1}}.

The non-vanishing is preserved under the regulator embedding into \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1}. \square

rem:calculus-up-to-epsilon:
Remark Calculus survives up to \varepsilon: derivatives, integrals, limits. While surreal numbers lack a Hilbert-space completion and canonical Lebesgue measure, a substantial fragment of differential and formal integral calculus lifts to \mathbf{No} up to an infinitesimal correction. This section records what works and how classical analysis is recovered via the standard-part map.

1. Differential calculus: Jackson derivative as the native d/dx Fix an infinitesimal \varepsilon \in \mathbf{No} with \varepsilon > 0 and set q = 1 + \varepsilon. The Jackson q-derivative

  d_q f(x) = \frac{f(q x) - f(x)}{(q - 1)\, x} = \frac{f((1+\varepsilon) x) - f(x)}{\varepsilon\, x}

is a native difference quotient on \mathbf{No}. Both numerator and denominator are surreals, and their ratio is well-defined wherever \varepsilon \, x \neq 0. For a standard function f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} lifted polynomially to \mathbf{No}, the classical derivative is recovered as

  \frac{df}{dx}(x_0) = \mathrm{st}\!\left(d_q f(x_0)\right) \qquad (x_0 \in \mathbb{R},\; q = 1 + \varepsilon).

The classical-limit functor, which breaks as an honest limit under surreal replacement, is replaced by the standard-part map composed with evaluation at a specific surreal q. More generally, Berarducci--Mantova (2018) construct a genuine derivation D : \mathbf{No} \to \mathbf{No} extending d/dx on \mathbb{R}, making \mathbf{No} a differential field. Many transcendental identities extend accordingly.

2. Formal integration: antiderivative exists, measure does not Berarducci--Mantova show that \mathbf{No} admits a right inverse to D. For every f \in \mathbf{No} there exists an antiderivative F with D(F) = f. This gives an honest indefinite integral \int f \, dx \in \mathbf{No} for every surreal function, up to a constant of integration.

A definite integral \int_a^b f \, dx agreeing with Lebesgue on \mathbb{R}-valued inputs does not exist. Use d_q as the native derivative and reserve \int for either the categorical Frobenius integral or the standard-part of Riemann sums computed on \mathbf{No}-valued partitions.

3. Limits become evaluations Every classical sequential limit L = \lim_{n \to \infty} a_n translates to L = \mathrm{st}(a_\omega), where \omega \in \mathbf{No} is the first infinite ordinal and a_\omega is the surreal obtained by transfer of the formula defining a_n. Limits become named values rather than formal processes. \lim_{q \to 1} becomes evaluation at q = 1 + \varepsilon, and the classical result is the standard-part. Double limits and iterated sup/inf over uncountable index sets require care.

4. Formal power series: the safe regime All formal-power-series identities used in the main paper (\exp_q, \log_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q, quantum dilogarithm, character generating functions) lift directly because they are manipulations in K[[x]] for K = \mathbf{No}. Convergence is replaced by formal convergence. The information-theory chapter computations survive: entropies, Lyapunov exponents, and bandwidth formulas are rational or formal-power-series expressions in q.

5. Measure up to \varepsilon: Loeb construction Given a hyperfinite partition of [0, 1] \subset \mathbf{No} into N = \omega equal subintervals, the counting measure divided by N gives a hyperfinite measure on [0,1]_{\mathbf{No}}. Its standard-part is Lebesgue measure on [0, 1] \subset \mathbb{R}. This Loeb measure is not canonical but behaves well for standard integrands. For the Möbius energy integral, one can define a Loeb measure on S^1 \times S^1 \subset \mathbf{No}^2, evaluate the integrand 1/|x - y|^2 against it, and take the standard-part after subtracting the regulariser. To infinitesimal precision, this yields the classical Möbius energy.

See Table.

For the aether-parameter q \to 1 limit, the surreal framework sharpens the theory by naming the infinitesimal regime explicitly. The absence of a canonical Lebesgue measure and a Hilbert completion is manageable because QOU uses neither in a load-bearing way: integration is categorical (Frobenius counit), decomposition is algebraic (Hoefsmit), and analytic-looking quantities (d_H(q), c_q, \hbar_q) are rational in q.

sec:surreal-construction-grading-intro: Conway's construction grades the surreals by birthday. This section connects the grading to the brane-tower level filtration.
def:birthday-grading:
Definition Birthday grading on a surreal-coefficient category. Let K be a real-closed field extending \mathbb{R} (typically K = \mathbf{No}, Conway's surreal numbers). The birthday b(x) \in \mathrm{Ord} of x \in \mathbf{No} is the least ordinal stage at which x is constructed in Conway's recursive \{L \mid R\} presentation.

Let \mathbf{C} be a K-linear category. The birthday grading on \mathbf{C} is the ordinal-indexed filtration of each hom-space

  \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(X, Y)_{\leq \alpha} = \bigl\{ f \in \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(X, Y) : \text{every coefficient of } f \text{ has birthday} \leq \alpha \bigr\}.
rem:birthday-grading-remark:
Remark Birthdays as sign-sequence lengths, and properties of the grading. Equivalently, the birthday b(x) is the length of the sign-sequence representation for x:

  b(0) = 0, \qquad b(n) = n \text{ for } n \in \mathbb{N}, \qquad b(\omega) = \omega, \qquad b(1/2) = 2, \qquad b(\pi) = \omega, \qquad b(\varepsilon) = \omega.

The birthday function refines the archimedean norm. Distinct reals x, y \in \mathbb{R} \subset \mathbf{No} have b(x), b(y) \leq \omega. The elements \varepsilon, \omega, and \omega^2 have progressively larger birthdays.

The birthday grading satisfies three properties:

  1. Exhaustiveness: \bigcup_\alpha \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(X, Y)_{\leq \alpha} = \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(X, Y).
  2. Composition: If f \in \mathrm{Hom}(X,Y)_{\leq \alpha} and g \in \mathrm{Hom}(Y,Z)_{\leq \beta}, then g \circ f \in \mathrm{Hom}(X,Z)_{\leq \alpha \oplus \beta} (where \oplus is the natural sum of ordinals).
  3. Monoidality: If \mathbf{C} is monoidal, f \otimes g \in \mathrm{Hom}(X \otimes X', Y \otimes Y')_{\leq \alpha \oplus \beta}.
rem:birthday-grading-archimedean:
Remark Birthday grading as a depth gauge and its archimedean sub-category. The birthday grading provides a coarse depth gauge for morphisms in surreal-enriched categories. It stratifies formal parameters into nested levels of infinitesimal and transfinite resolution. Statements with hom-coefficients of birthday < \omega involve only dyadic rationals. Birthday-\leq \omega statements include limit reals and first-order infinitesimals. Birthday > \omega statements use named infinities like \omega or transseries terms like \log \omega.

The sub-category defined by b(f) \leq \omega forms the archimedean-coefficient sub-category. Its morphisms have coefficients that are real numbers or bounded infinitesimals. For \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbf{No}}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) with q \in \mathbb{R} \subset \mathbf{No}, this recovers \mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)). The arithmetic of \mathbf{No} restricted to birthday \leq \omega coincides with \mathbb{R} exactly on the archimedean part.
ex:birthday-grading-aether:
Example Birthday of the aether parameters c_q, \hbar_q, d_H(q) at q = 1 + \varepsilon. Consider the aether parameter q = 1 + \varepsilon for an infinitesimal \varepsilon \in \mathbf{No} with b(\varepsilon) = \omega. Its sign sequence (+, -, -, -, \ldots) has length 1 + \omega = \omega. The associated parameters resolve as follows:

  • c_q = 1/(q - 1) = 1/\varepsilon = \omega has birthday \omega.
  • \hbar_q = (q-1)/q = \varepsilon(1 + \varepsilon)^{-1} has birthday \omega.
  • d_H(q) = (2q-1)^2/q^3 = (1 + 2\varepsilon)^2(1 + \varepsilon)^{-3} has birthday \omega.

Expressions rational in q evaluated at q = 1 + \varepsilon remain in the birthday-\leq \omega stratum, embedding into the Laurent-series field \mathbb{R}(\!(\varepsilon)\!). The standard-part map distinguishes between finite and infinitesimal within this stratum. The birthday alone does not, as limit reals like \pi also have birthday \omega.
def:sign-sequence-of-braid:
Definition Sign-sequence functor B_n \to \mathbf{No} via Hecke eigenspaces. Let V be the fundamental representation of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), and let \beta = \sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k} be a braid word in B_n. Fix a standard tableau t of shape \lambda \vdash n with \ell(\lambda) \leq 2. The sign-sequence surreal \mathrm{surr}(\beta, t) \in \mathbf{No} of \beta at t is constructed as follows.

The Hecke representation \rho_n : B_n \to H_n(q) sends each \sigma_i^{\pm 1} to \sigma_i^{\pm 1}. The Hoefsmit seminormal vector v_t \in S_\lambda at t is an eigenvector of every Young--Jucys--Murphy element. The braid \beta acts on v_t by successively decomposing \rho(\sigma_{i_j}^{\epsilon_j})\, v_{t_j} into symmetric and antisymmetric components, recording s_j = + for the symmetric component and s_j = - for the antisymmetric. The resulting sign sequence s = (s_1, \ldots, s_k) defines the finite-birthday surreal \mathrm{surr}(\beta, t) := \mathrm{Gonshor}(s) \in \mathbf{No}, where \mathrm{Gonshor}: \{+, -\}^* \to \mathbf{No} is the canonical sign-sequence-to-surreal map.
rem:sign-sequence-of-braid-remark: Remark Multiplicativity and tableau independence of the sign-sequence surreal. For each fixed standard tableau t, the sign-sequence surreal assignment \mathrm{surr}(-, t) : B_n \to \mathbf{No} is a multiplicative monoid map: \mathrm{surr}(\beta_1 \beta_2, t) is computed by first applying \beta_2's sign sequence at t to obtain t', then concatenating with \beta_1's sign sequence at t'. Changing the tableau permutes the sign sequence by a Young--Jucys--Murphy permutation. Quotienting by this action gives a tableau-independent functor \widetilde{\mathrm{surr}} : B_n \longrightarrow \mathbf{No} / \sim.
rem:sign-sequence-of-braid-invariant:
Remark The sign-sequence functor as a transfinite refinement of the crossing number. A surreal number x \in \mathbf{No} admits a canonical sign-sequence presentation: a function s_x : \alpha \to \{+, -\} for some ordinal \alpha = b(x). The sequence encodes Conway's \{L \mid R\} construction step-by-step: at stage \beta < \alpha, s_x(\beta) = + means "x is the rightmost option", and s_x(\beta) = - means "leftmost option". Hecke generators have two eigenvalues, q (symmetric channel) and -q^{-1} (antisymmetric channel) (Hoefsmit seminormal form). This binary choice at each level is exactly the sign-sequence data, providing a canonical functor from braid words to surreals.

The sign sequence has length equal to the crossing number c(\beta), so b(\mathrm{surr}(\beta, t)) \leq c(\beta). Equality holds when the braid is reduced. This cleanly refines the crossing-number invariant by an ordinal-valued quantity.

The sign sequence carries strictly more information than the crossing number: it records which eigenchannel is chosen at each crossing. Distinct braids with the same crossing number generally give distinct surreals. Surrealisation is a stronger braid invariant valued in \mathbf{No} / \sim. It is the precise sense in which "Hoefsmit seminormal form is the surreal \{L \mid R\} construction".
prop:hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction:
Proposition Hoefsmit seminormal form is Conway's \{L \mid R\} construction. The Hoefsmit seminormal form (Hoefsmit seminormal form) diagonalises H_n(q) on V^{\otimes n} along a Young--Jucys--Murphy tower indexed by standard tableaux, each generator \sigma_i splitting a tableau-vector into a symmetric (q-eigen) and an antisymmetric (-q^{-1}-eigen) component. Writing \mathrm{Tab}(\lambda) for the standard tableaux of shape \lambda and \mathbf{No}_{\leq n}^{\mathrm{dy}} for the dyadic surreals of birthday \leq n, there is a canonical injective embedding

  \Phi : \bigsqcup_{\lambda \vdash n,\, \ell(\lambda) \leq 2} \mathrm{Tab}(\lambda) \hookrightarrow \mathbf{No}_{\leq n}^{\mathrm{dy}}

such that:

  1. The empty tableau at n = 0 and the singleton tableau at n = 1 both map to 0. For n \geq 2, the one-row tableau (n) maps to a non-zero value determined by its sign sequence.
  2. Each YJM-edge t \to t' in the tableau forest corresponds to a unique sign-sequence extension s \to s\!\cdot\! + (symmetric channel) or s \to s\!\cdot\! - (antisymmetric channel). The sign sequence of a size-n tableau has length n - 1.
  3. The birthday b(\Phi(t)) is bounded by the length of the sign sequence (i.e., by n - 1). Surreals in the image are of birthday \leq n - 1. The complement of the image in \mathbf{No}_{\leq n}^{\mathrm{dy}} consists of non-tableau dyadic rationals.

The eigencomponent recursion, the tableau-forest counting, and the consequences of this identification (birthday-refined crossing number, the Conway-recipe form of \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i), and the surreal sign-sequence expansion of J_K(q)) are recorded in the context note.
conj:jones-birthday:
Conjecture Birthday refinement of the Jones polynomial. The Jones polynomial J_K(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] is the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho_n(\beta)) of the Hecke representation of any braid word \beta whose closure is the oriented link K. The Markov trace is computed by summing contributions from every standard tableau t of every two-rowed shape \lambda \vdash n.

By Hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction, each tableau t corresponds to a finite-dyadic surreal \Phi(t) \in \mathbf{No} of birthday \leq n. This suggests that the Jones polynomial admits a birthday refinement: a finer invariant that records contributions stratified by the birthday of the underlying surreal sign sequence.

There exists a refinement \widetilde{J}_K \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]^{\mathrm{Ord}} satisfying:

  1. Recovery of Jones: \sum_\alpha \widetilde{J}_K(\alpha) = J_K(q).
  2. Birthday locality: \widetilde{J}_K(\alpha) depends only on tableau contributions of YJM depth \leq \alpha.
  3. Strict refinement: there exist knots K_1, K_2 with J_{K_1}(q) = J_{K_2}(q) but \widetilde{J}_{K_1} \neq \widetilde{J}_{K_2}.

If (3) holds, \widetilde{J}_K is a strictly stronger invariant than the Jones polynomial, contradicting the classical view that all braid-word information is collapsed by the Markov trace.

The Jones polynomial loses information due to Markov-trace averaging and tableau-shape averaging. The birthday refinement preserves the trace-type averaging but stratifies by YJM depth, a finer invariant than the shape. Contributions from early symmetric channels are separated from contributions from late symmetric channels. Precedents exist: Khovanov homology categorifies the Jones polynomial and is strictly stronger. The birthday refinement exposes previously hidden tableau-level data.

To prove the conjecture, it suffices to produce two knots with identical Jones polynomials and distinct birthday refinements. To disprove it, it suffices to show that the YJM-depth filtration of any tableau contributes only via its endpoint (the shape \lambda). The proposed test is the Conway--Kinoshita pair (11n34, 11n42).

The conjecture remains open. The Hoefsmit eigenchannel data is explicit, so the refinement is computable. A direct computational attack involves computing \widetilde{J}_K for 11n34 and 11n42. For each YJM-extension path \pi of length 11, compute the Hoefsmit matrix product, convert to a sign sequence, and compute the Gonshor surreal. Aggregate contributions by b(\mathrm{Gonshor}(\pi)) to yield \widetilde{J}_K. If \widetilde{J}_{11n34} \neq \widetilde{J}_{11n42}, the conjecture is established. This requires Hoefsmit matrix entries for H_{11}(q), the gonshor map, and a script computing matrix products along YJM paths. Falsification requires proving the Hoefsmit-trajectory sum factors through the YJM endpoint.
rem:hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction-con:
Remark Hoefsmit-as-surreal — eigencomponent recursion, tableau counting, and consequences. At each step of the Young--Jucys--Murphy tower, a Hecke generator \sigma_i splits a tableau-vector into two eigencomponents:

  • the symmetric (q-eigen) component, corresponding to the tableau where boxes i and i+1 lie in the same row;
  • the antisymmetric (-q^{-1}-eigen) component, corresponding to the tableau where they lie in the same column.

This is structurally identical to Conway's recursive surreal construction.

Let \mathrm{Tab}(\lambda) denote the set of standard tableaux of shape \lambda, viewed as the vertex set of a tree \mathcal{T}_n whose edges record the Young--Jucys--Murphy ordering. Let \mathbf{No}_{= n}^{\mathrm{dy}} denote the set of dyadic surreals of birthday exactly n (equivalently, sign sequences of length n). The number of two-rowed standard tableaux of size n is \binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}; the number of dyadic surreals of birthday exactly n is 2^n. The embedding \Phi of Hoefsmit seminormal form is Conway's \{L \mid R\} construction is an injective embedding, not a bijection of forests.

This identification has several immediate consequences. The sign-sequence braid invariant is well-defined and lives in \mathbf{No}_{\leq c(\beta)}^{\mathrm{dy}} for a braid \beta of crossing number c(\beta). Birthday refines crossing number: b(\mathrm{surr}(\beta, t)) \leq c(\beta), with equality for reduced braids. The Hoefsmit factorisation equals the Conway construction: the closed formula for \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) as a 2 \times 2 matrix in YJM coordinates is exactly the recursive surreal recipe x = \{x^- \mid x^+\}, with the eigenvalue ratio q : -q^{-1} determining the position of x. The Jones polynomial J_K(q) can be re-expressed as a weighted sum over surreal sign sequences (Jones polynomial birthday refinement). Finally, knot complexity acquires an honest ordinal-valued refinement: knots of unbounded crossing number live at birthdays approaching \omega.

The Hoefsmit seminormal form is already the algebraic-combinatorial backbone of the paper. This same backbone is shown to be a literal instance of Conway's surreal-number construction. The surreal lift of QOU is not a new structure; it is a different language for what Hoefsmit already provides.
prf:hoefsmit-is-surreal-construction:
Proof Proof of hoefsmit is surreal construction. Sketch.

The Hoefsmit seminormal basis is built by inductively decomposing V^{\otimes n} via the chain H_1(q) \subset H_2(q) \subset \cdots \subset H_n(q). At each step k, every existing eigenvector v_t for H_k(q) splits under \sigma_k into:

  • a^+_t \cdot v_{t \cup \square_{k+1}^{\to}} (extend tableau rightward; q-eigenvalue);
  • a^-_t \cdot v_{t \cup \square_{k+1}^{\downarrow}} (extend tableau downward; -q^{-1}-eigenvalue).

Conway's surreal construction at stage k takes each existing surreal x with sign-sequence s and produces exactly two new surreals: x^+ (insert + at position k+1) and x^- (insert - at position k+1). The embedding \Phi matches each tableau splitting with the corresponding sign extension step-by-step. The tableau side, however, produces the antisymmetric child only when the two-row shape constraint permits it (a box can be added to the second row of \lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) only if \lambda_2 < \lambda_1), while Conway's construction always splits both ways — which is exactly why \Phi is injective but not surjective: the unmatched sign sequences are the non-tableau dyadic rationals identified in the statement.

Compatibility with sums is forced by the eigenvalue convention: \sigma_i's q-eigenspace + -q^{-1}-eigenspace decomposition matches Conway's \{L \mid R\} pairing L < x < R.

For tableaux of shape \lambda with \ell(\lambda) \leq 2, the restriction to "first or second row" is exactly the \mathrm{SU}(2) constraint that limits Young diagrams to two-rowed shapes — giving the binary (rather than r-ary) split needed for the sign-sequence interpretation.

A full proof requires:

  • making the YJM-tableau tree structure precise (Young tableaux together with a successor relation);
  • a precise treatment of Gonshor's sign-sequence-to-surreal map;
  • checking the eigenvalue conventions (Hoefsmit uses q and -q^{-1}; Conway's construction uses left/right of midpoint).

The embedding (sign sequence functor) is therefore taken as a hypothesis pending these prerequisites.
